adapt.when: You’re new to a project, returning after changes, or missing facts needed for the next task.
adapt.adds: Reads the relevant code, project rules, and prior decisions. It hands back verified context for the next step without editing the project.
adapt.prompt: Use Mirket Adapt to trace how CSV exports are queued and generated in this repo. Point me to the key files and decisions. Don’t change anything.

architect.when: You’re making a technical choice that will shape how parts of the system fit together.
architect.adds: Compares viable options against real constraints and shows the tradeoffs. It records the rationale once a lasting decision is settled.
architect.prompt: Use Mirket Architect to compare generating exports inside the web service with moving them to a worker. Weigh failure recovery and ownership, then recommend an option.

audit.when: You need a review of a patch, plan, or system before deciding what to change or accept.
audit.adds: Reports material defects, risks, and improvements with evidence and a next step. It names gaps in the review and leaves edits to the owner.
audit.prompt: Use Mirket Audit to review this pagination patch. Check empty pages, duplicate records, and compatibility with existing callers. Report findings without editing.

author.when: You’re writing or reviewing docs, product copy, or issue reports.
author.adds: Turns source material into clear writing for the intended reader. It checks claims against evidence and makes the next action easy to find.
author.prompt: Use Mirket Author to turn this export bug report into a ticket. Separate confirmed reproduction steps from what still needs checking.

brief.when: You’re pausing work, resuming it, or handing it to another person or agent.
brief.adds: Captures the exact next action, what’s already approved, and the evidence worth carrying forward. It identifies which facts to recheck before resuming.
brief.prompt: Use Mirket Brief to hand off the paused export fix. Include the approved scope, the reproduction command, and the first check the next agent should run.

clean.when: You’re tidying up or reviewing what should go into an authorized commit.
clean.adds: Checks which files are verified leftovers and which changes belong in the delivery. It protects unrelated work and keeps private scratch files out of the commit.
clean.prompt: Use Mirket Clean to review this staged patch. Flag generated files, stale links, and any unrelated edits that should stay out of the commit.

code.when: You’re implementing or reviewing a change in a known language, framework, or database.
code.adds: Brings in patterns and pitfalls for the versions actually in use. It helps the agent choose readable code and checks that fit the change.
code.prompt: Use Mirket Code to review this Next.js settings page. Check what belongs on the server and where client interactivity is needed.

debug.when: Something fails or behaves differently from what you expected.
debug.adds: Starts from the observed failure, tests plausible causes, and narrows the fix to what the evidence supports.
debug.prompt: Use Mirket Debug to find why CSV exports time out at 10,000 rows. Reproduce the failure, fix the cause, and rerun the same case.

deploy.when: You’re rolling out a change, checking a live service, or recovering from an incident.
deploy.adds: Pins the exact release and environment, verifies what’s actually running, and defines when to stop or roll back.
deploy.prompt: Use Mirket Deploy to roll v1.8.2 out to staging. Verify sign-in and CSV export there. Roll back if either check fails.

design.when: You’re creating, revising, or reviewing an interface or other visual work.
design.adds: Sets a direction that fits the brief, then checks how the result looks and behaves in its intended setting.
design.prompt: Use Mirket Design to simplify the export settings dialog. Keep its behavior intact and check the finished design at desktop and narrow mobile widths.

equip.when: You need to choose a tool or format, or decide whether an existing one is worth keeping.
equip.adds: Compares the options against the actual task and the cost of switching. It identifies what would justify a change.
equip.prompt: Use Mirket Equip to compare CSV and XLSX for sharing monthly reports with finance. Check compatibility and maintenance cost before recommending a format.

execute.when: Use it throughout Mirket work, from routine fixes to larger tasks.
execute.adds: Keeps the agent on the simplest path that meets the request. It checks what matters and reports the result without narrating every step.
execute.prompt: Use Mirket Execute to correct the CSV download label. Keep the change focused, verify it in the dialog, and tell me the result.

market.when: You’re positioning an offer, shaping its message, or planning how to reach people.
market.adds: Uses audience evidence to choose what to say, where to say it, and what action to ask for. It keeps claims tied to what you can support.
market.prompt: Use Mirket Market to draft a launch email for scheduled exports. Use the attached customer interviews to pick one benefit and one call to action.

migrate.when: You’re changing stored data, schemas, or configuration and need to preserve what already matters.
migrate.adds: Spells out what must survive, sequences the transition around existing readers and writers, and checks that recovery is workable.
migrate.prompt: Use Mirket Migrate to rehearse renaming the customer status field with anonymized staging data. Check that older readers still work and that the previous state can be restored.

plan.when: A task has dependencies, meaningful risk, or work that several people or agents need to coordinate.
plan.adds: Turns the agreed outcome into ordered steps with owners, checks, and a record of progress.
plan.prompt: Use Mirket Plan to sequence the move to background exports. Identify which work can run in parallel, the integration checks, and the rollback point. Stop at the plan.

preflight.when: A tool won’t run, or you need to know whether an environment can support the task.
preflight.adds: Checks the actual setup and separates blockers from capabilities that already work. It gives you the smallest check or fix needed to move forward.
preflight.prompt: Use Mirket Preflight to check why the browser tests won’t start in CI. Identify the missing or incompatible prerequisite before changing the setup.

refactor.when: Existing code is hard to change, but its observable behavior should stay the same.
refactor.adds: Finds a simpler structure and uses focused before-and-after checks to catch changes callers would notice.
refactor.prompt: Use Mirket Refactor to consolidate the two CSV formatting paths. Keep column order, escaping, and output bytes the same for both callers.

search.when: You need evidence from outside the project, such as community practice, competing products, or historical context.
search.adds: Follows leads into primary sources and shows what they support. It separates verified findings from inference and notes missing evidence.
search.prompt: Use Mirket Search to compare how three open-source CLI projects communicate breaking changes. Cite release notes and maintainer discussions, and explain where their practices differ.

ship.when: You’re deciding what to build, what to launch, or whether a release helped users.
ship.adds: Connects user evidence to priorities, requirements, and measures of success. It makes the tradeoffs clear so you can make the product call.
ship.prompt: Use Mirket Ship to rank saved filters, bulk edits, and scheduled exports using the attached support tickets. Recommend what to build first and how we’d measure success.

test.when: You need evidence that a change works, a regression stays fixed, or a performance claim holds.
test.adds: Chooses checks that can expose meaningful failures and reports what passed, what failed, and what remains unverified.
test.prompt: Use Mirket Test to verify the CSV escaping fix. Cover quotes, commas, and newlines with a real download, then report what passed and any gaps.
